previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), inactive IBD, celiac disease, and hypertension was admitted for acute right upper quadrant abdominal pain and fever. Initial evaluation revealed elevated liver enzymes and gallstones without cholecystitis on ultrasound. An MRCP showed progression of PSC with active bile duct inflammation but no malignancy or obstruction. She was treated with intravenous antibiotics, later transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin, and her symptoms improved significantly. She remained stable throughout the hospitalization, with no complications, and was discharged home with a 12-day course of antibiotics and instructions to follow up with her gastroenterologist in two weeks.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ with history of PSC complicated by 
cirrhosis, recurrent episodes of cholangitis, presenting with 
RUQ pain, fever, elevated transaminases and lipase.

Active Issues:
#Recurrent cholangitis: Similar to prior episodes, patient was 
previously treated with Meropenem.  She did not have a 
leukocytosis on admission but did have fever to 101.7 on 
admission. Initially, RUQ U/S showed results c/w prior imaging 
but after further review, seemed that there was evidence of a 
more proximal stricture that would be amenable to ERCP.  The 
patient was started on Meropenem 500mg q6hrs.  Her fevers 
resolved and her abdominal pain improved.  She went for ERCP on 
___ which showed no stricture or stone amenable to endoscopic 
therapy.  Her diet was advanced post procedure and she tolerated 
this well.  She had a PICC line placed on ___ for completion of 
a course of IV antibiotics with Ertapenem given the ease of once 
daily dosing. She will complete an additional five days of 
antibiotics at discharge and was given a prescription for 
Rifaximin to begin after the Ertapenem.

#Diarrhea: Patient with diarrhea for past few weeks in setting 
of antibiotics use. Unclear whether this represents side effect 
from medications vs. C. difficile but story more consistent with 
chronic symptoms.  C.diff negative this admission.

Chronic Issues:
#PSC: Known PSC complicated by cirrhosis (stage III-IV in 
___. She has known 3 cords of grade I varices from an EGD 
___. She has been maintained on furosemide for fluid 
retention.  Patient is due for colonoscopy which she will 
schedule as outpatient. 
 
#Hypertension  Lisinopril held on admission for concern of 
sepsis.  Restarted home dose upon discharge.

#Hypothyroidism: Continued home levothyroxine  

#GERD: Continued home omeprazole  

Transitional Issues:
